Clear Lake Walleye and Pike Fishing, Riding Mountain

Clear Lake in Riding Mountain National Park holds walleye and northern pike. You need the park’s fishing permit; a Manitoba provincial licence does not cover this water. Check the park’s fishing season and boat requirements before travel. Choose your target fish first, then confirm a permitted access point and suitable tackle.

What should you know about this water?

Updated 2026-11-21

Clear Lake in Riding Mountain National Park holds walleye and northern pike. You need the park’s fishing permit; a Manitoba provincial licence does not cover this water. Check the park’s fishing season and boat requirements before travel. Choose your target fish first, then confirm a permitted access point and suitable tackle.

Parks Canada describes Clear Lake as a low-nutrient lake with clear water and fourteen fish species. Walleye and pike share the lake with whitefish, white sucker and slimy sculpin. That variety does not mean one setup suits every fish. Tell your fishing partner which species you intend to pursue before you divide the tackle or decide how to spend the day.

Build time into the plan for the park’s current watercraft requirements. Keep the fishing permit separate from the boat arrangements when you make your checklist. Check the latest park bulletin before you leave, rather than relying on last year’s access details. If your plans change to another lake, check that water separately and confirm how you must clean and move the gear.

Does a Manitoba licence cover Clear Lake?

No. Parks Canada requires its national park fishing permit.

Which two fish does this trip focus on?

Walleye and northern pike. Both occur in the park’s Clear Lake species list.

Should I use last year’s boat instructions?

No. Check the current park access bulletin before travel.

Can I assume another park lake has the same season?

No. Check the named water on the park’s current fishing rules page.

What should I put on my trip checklist?

The park permit, target fish, tackle, access arrangements and a weather alternative.

SEASON

When this trip makes sense.

Parks Canada lists Clear Lake’s fishing season as May 15 to March 31, with weekend adjustments stated on its rules page. Check current closures before travel. A winter opening does not establish safe ice.

LICENCE & PERMITS

Fishing licence for Canada national parks fishing permit

Anglers need a Parks Canada fishing permit where national park fishing is allowed. A provincial or territorial licence does not replace it, and permit coverage varies by park.

  • 1 day$15 CAD
  • Annual$51.25 CAD

Buy a national park fishing permit in person at a Parks Canada visitor centre. Jasper also sells at its Information Centre, campground kiosks (Whistlers, Wapiti, Miette) and local tackle shops. A park entry pass is also required.

Go to the official site ↗Canada national parks fishing permit licence steps

Permits for this trip

  • National park fishing permit ↗
    Anglers aged 16 and over; younger anglers share the accompanying permit holder’s limit. Obtain the park permit at a park office or authorized outlet.
  • Aquatic invasive species watercraft permit ↗
    Visitors who bring watercraft or regulated water equipment to Clear Lake. Obtain a staff inspection and annual permit before launch.

Rules for this water

  • A Manitoba licence does not cover Clear Lake inside Riding Mountain National Park.
  • Use barbless hooks; lead tackle under 50 g is prohibited.
  • Use one line; fishing is closed from two hours after sunset until one hour before sunrise.
  • Clear Lake is open May 15–March 31; swimming areas and marinas are closed to fishing.
  • Watercraft and specified equipment require an aquatic invasive species inspection and annual permit.
